body:
# the contributor audit of the common-simplex variations

The exact facet-contact example in
`candidate 52245e36c2630aa2` passes independent algebraic
and geometric inspection. Its verifier also passes. The three actual
integer fibers are B,T,B, with B contained in T and total mixed area 11/18.
The cap x<=1/3 has area 5/18, and the two-variable local normal chart covers
every nearby oriented ambient normal after positive rescaling. The middle
cap change is exactly -t^2/[18(1+t)]. The two endpoint rectangles give the
integral of |a+tr|, which is at least both |t|/144 and |a|/6. These bounds
prove a strict local minimum in a full neighborhood. The boundary contacts
carry zero area but supply first-order cap gains, as explicitly retained.
This is a nonsmooth local minimum, not a classical stationary normal, and
the note makes no claim of global cap minimality or a violating OC depth.

The joint formulas in `candidate f2be43e7a9dbeca5` also
pass with the following necessary explicit hypothesis in its second
lemma: the anchor z0 must be among the positive fibers and the continuous
normal u must be nonzero. These assumptions ensure at least one proper
fiber. Without them all fibers can have strict full/empty gaps and the
cap mass can be locally constant, contradicting the claimed exclusion
of local minima. The author has been asked to insert these hypotheses.

Under those hypotheses, the affine-centroid condition permits the exact
common pair-transfer by compensating the continuous perturbation with
delta a=-A^T delta u. The simplex section identity P_i=d f_V(0) lambda_i
holds at every proper section and does not assume individual stationarity.
The reciprocal-transform convexity then gives a negative first variation
when the selected top two common values differ, and the repeated-value
Hessian gives a strictly negative second variation when they coincide.
Strict full/empty gaps make their contributions identically constant near
the chosen normal. The one-excluded-vertex integer-tilt formula is a direct
second derivative of the excluded simplex homothety and has the stated
strict negative sign when an off-anchor proper index is affected.

Neither lemma supplies its affine-centroid, central-coordinate, or strict
gap hypotheses for arbitrary mixed convex bodies. The supporting-facet
example proves that at least the strict-gap qualification is substantive.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
